executiveSummary: GM0758 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, 188,779 residents, 56 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, 24 BRT settlements, two ProRail stations, 237 transit stop areas and ten NWB-derived intermunicipal corridors are coherent; official nulls, zero-intensity behavior, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, event-attributable essential-service person-hours and map-layer invariance also pass. Release remains correction-required for three reproducible spatial contradictions. A three-line Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity screen converts Breda's real but mechanism-specific Bovenmark, Aa of Weerijs and Mark-Dintel flood context into a persistent citywide 100% normalized inundation-stress display without a selected hydraulic event. One common neighbourhood hash gives river, pluvial and heat exactly the same rank order even though Breda publishes event-specific water-depth and heat surfaces with materially different point samples. A focused T+24 ignition inside an official TOP10NL needle-forest polygon in BU07580309 Mastbos makes that source neighbourhood rank only 48th of 56. Breda offers unusually actionable public correction data through its ArcGIS climate services and Brabantse Delta WMS/WFS/FeatureServer routes, but event definitions, edition, licence and no-data must be retained and observed/context layers must never be presented as the simulated scenario clock. Utility topology, live condition, backup, stock, crew and restoration data remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented; all eight service graphs correctly call their shared road corridors logical transfer proxies.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027
supports: The formally adopted strategic profile ranks extreme weather and nature fire among the five most probable regional categories and flooding and digital vital-infrastructure disruption among the five highest-impact categories.

It distinguishes coastal/transition, major-river, regional-defence and freely inundating brook-valley mechanisms and explicitly identifies the Bovenmark and Aa of Weerijs at Breda; the Mark-Dintel system has separate regional water-defence context.

It covers heavy rain, drought, heat, cold, snow, ice and storm; forest/fire fuel, access and extinguishing-water constraints; eastern-regional earthquake potential; hazardous-material road/rail/pipeline transport; and cascades across electricity, drinking water, wastewater, gas, telecom/ICT, mobility, facilities and supply.

The profile is qualitative strategic context renewed at least once every four years, not a live warning, local incident footprint, probability/depth raster, asset inventory or restoration commitment; no machine API or explicit redistribution licence accompanies the PDF.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatportaal De Baronie — Wateroverlast ArcGIS MapServer
supports: The public EPSG:28992 service exposes JSON/GeoJSON/PBF feature queries and map/identify operations for middle/high-voltage stations, telecom antennas, vulnerable objects, emergency-service locations, road passability and a 3Di/AHN3 maximum-water-depth raster.

Road classes encode up to 10 cm as generally passable, 10–30 cm as emergency-traffic-only and 30 cm or more as impassable, making this an integration-ready scenario surface for mobility/response-access tests rather than current road state.

The raster layer name says 70 mm in one hour while its description says T100, 57 mm in 60 minutes. That published event-definition conflict must be resolved before calibration; the described 0.25 m2 result resolution must be retained as publisher wording rather than silently reinterpreted.

A diagnostic identify at each of 56 CBS neighbourhood reference points returns water 0.555972 at Nieuw Wolfslaar and 0.062238 at Sportpark, with NoData at 34 points. These are point samples, not neighbourhood means or observations; NoData is not zero. The service metadata states neither a fixed refresh cadence nor a blanket reuse licence, so cache/reuse rights and edition must be cleared.

evidenceSources.title: Markdal-Noord, regional defences and machine-readable water registers

The Mark-Dintel-Vliet regional-defence project in Breda and neighbouring municipalities was completed on 9 October 2024. Presence or completion of a defence is not a failure scenario, exceedance probability, depth, arrival, duration or guaranteed performance.

The water board publishes current WMS/WFS/download routes at https://geoservices.brabantsedelta.nl/arcgis/rest/services/EXTERN and says the services expose the latest register version; its metadata gives no fixed cadence or blanket licence. National HWH OGC services https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken is published weekly while DAMO cadence/contributor completeness varies.

The current generalized-boundary snapshot contains 232 display-only objects: two sewer pumps, RWZI Nieuwveer, 29 surface-water pumps and 200 weirs. Object presence is context, not hydraulic connectivity, capacity, control state, emergency power or first-72-hour performance.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0758 pnpm audit:model passed both focused coverage tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 30.54 seconds (30.34 seconds test execution) on the final rerun.
Every preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every required checkpoint.

Repeated frames are deterministic; outputs are finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity; all eight headline pressure weights participate and close to one.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles population 188,779, affected population 127,951 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum observed floating-point discrepancy 2.84e-14.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The major-river proximity screen, shared neighbourhood allocator and source-insensitive wildfire map contradict Breda's public hydraulic, climate and forest evidence.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-469 derives Rhine/Meuse/IJssel exposure only from municipality-reference-point distance to three approximate line segments; GM0758 is inside its 50 km support although no selected Mark/Bovenmark/Aa/defence/breach depth, arrival, duration or recession surface is supplied.

At T+24 and T+72 the river preset retains internal depth-like proxy 2.601148 and severity 0.819592. The UI transforms that proxy by /1.5 and clamps it to 100% inundation stress; modeled people under pressure are 114,896 then 118,820 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours 1,818,482 then 7,041,187.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3517-3531 applies the same seeded neighbourhood multiplier to every hazard. River, pluvial and heat therefore have the identical top-five T+24 order: Sportpark, Liesbos, Buitengebied Teteringen, Overkroeten and Gageldonk.

E04/E05 provide different local water and PET surfaces. Reference-point identify instead yields the largest sampled water value at Nieuw Wolfslaar 0.555972 and largest PET at Brabantpark 50.967907; Sportpark is 0.062238 water and 46.111282 PET. These point samples are diagnostic rather than neighbourhood aggregates, but they falsify any claim that one common order was source-derived.

A focused synthetic T+24 source [4.753355365563599, 51.55111907561502] intersects official TOP10NL needle forest and BU07580309 Mastbos. Direct fire is 0.524418 and municipality severity 0.530306, but Mastbos ranks 48th at 0.474222 while Sportpark ranks first at 0.625703.
River emits derived-screening and pluvial/heat/wildfire emit synthetic evidence, so these maps must not support neighbourhood dispatch, evacuation or resource-priority claims.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve confidence, dependency order, scenario operations and counterfactual scope.

System-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, summing to one.

River power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/supply availability stays 0.446070/0.437594/0.249669/0.694058/0.442920/0.262855/0.391027 from T+24 to T+72, while facilities declines from 0.485865 to 0.380508 through dependency dynamics.

Other preset recovery curves are bounded scenario assumptions. They must not be shown as Breda provider, hospital, transport or water-board restoration forecasts.

findings.summary: A coarse named-major-river proximity field turns Breda's distinct Bovenmark/Aa/Mark-Dintel mechanisms into unsupported persistent citywide maximum inundation stress.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-469 uses only municipality-reference-point distance to three approximate Rhine/Meuse/IJssel segments. At T+24 and T+72 the canonical river preset reports internal depth-like proxy 2.601148, displayed after /1.5 clamping as 100% normalized inundation stress, severity 0.819592 and zero recovery for all services; modeled people under pressure are 114,896 then 118,820 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours 1,818,482 then 7,041,187. E03 identifies genuine but different freely inundating Bovenmark/Aa of Weerijs valleys and regional Mark-Dintel mechanisms; E06 identifies specific channels, storage, controls and completed regional defences. No selected connected event, defence state, breach, water level, depth, arrival, duration or recession surface supports the displayed municipality-wide amplitude. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared proximity-screen defect, not a claim that Breda is flood-safe.
findings.action: Render the current direct GM0758 river result Unknown/numerically neutral pending an expert-selected, named and versioned connected hydraulic event. Preserve separately labeled Bovenmark/Aa brook-valley, Mark-Dintel regional-defence, pluvial, control/storage and indirect transport/supply pathways; do not convert unavailable scenario coverage to zero or safety.

findings.summary: One shared neighbourhood hash makes Breda river, pluvial and heat maps exactly rank-identical despite authoritative event-specific water and heat surfaces.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3517-3531 seeds the same regional multiplier from city/scenario/region for every physical hazard. River, pluvial and heat therefore rank Sportpark, Liesbos, Buitengebied Teteringen, Overkroeten and Gageldonk first through fifth. E04/E05 expose municipality-scale water and PET surfaces. Diagnostic ArcGIS identify at the 56 neighbourhood reference points instead returns maximum sampled water 0.555972 at Nieuw Wolfslaar and maximum PET 50.967907 at Brabantpark, versus Sportpark 0.062238 water and 46.111282 PET; 34 water and 19 PET points return NoData. Point identifies are not zonal means or observations, but they show the common order is not source-derived. The water raster also conflicts internally between a 70 mm/h label and T100 57 mm/60 min description.
findings.action: Mark local water/heat ranks unsupported until source-specific surfaces are integrated. Resolve the published rainfall-event definition with Breda, pin layer/version/reference date/scenario/units/resolution/uncertainty/licence and compute geometry-aware zonal values with typed NoData; never turn NoData into zero or mix 2050 context with the synthetic T+0–72 clock.

findings.summary: An explicit ignition inside Mastbos does not control the neighbourhood map presented as local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies TOP10NL needle-forest object 105903867 and diagnostic source [4.753355365563599, 51.55111907561502] inside BU07580309 Mastbos; E07 independently lists Mastbos as provincial nature-fire management area 5. A focused synthetic T+24 run reports direct fire 0.524418, smoke 0.512453, drought 0.593431 and municipality severity 0.530306, yet Mastbos ranks 48th at 0.474222 while Sportpark ranks first at 0.625703. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:879-895 computes municipality reference-point distance and model.ts:3517-3531 never intersects the neighbourhood source, perimeter or eligible fuel. This diagnostic is not an observed fire or forecast.
findings.action: Keep direct-fire neighbourhood ranks visibly synthetic/unsupported and prohibit operational rank use. Make local allocation source/perimeter and eligible-fuel aware, while modeling transported smoke, drought, wind, access, extinguishing water and suppression assumptions separately.

findings.summary: Public water and climate objects improve Breda context but do not establish urban-drainage connectivity, capacity, control state or restoration.
findings.evidence: E06 contributes two sewer pumps, RWZI Nieuwveer, 29 surface-water pumps and 200 weirs; E04 adds modeled water depth, vulnerable assets and road passability. The application correctly marks all 232 water objects affectsSimulation=false. Compound T+24/T+72 drainage availability 0.318303 arises from generic equations, not catchment/pipeline connectivity, inlet blockage, storage, pump/weir capacity, receiving-water level, controls, emergency power or telemetry. HWH/DAMO and Brabantse Delta register coverage is contributor/object context, while a complete municipal GWSW/native sewer graph was not found; absence is Unknown.
findings.action: Keep IMWA/DAMO/water-board objects as non-causal context. Obtain a licensed, security-reviewed municipal GWSW/native drainage and stress-test export before causal use; otherwise expose named bounded subsystem assumptions with connectivity, capacity, backup and current state explicitly Unknown.

findings.summary: The same ten road corridors are cloned across all eight services and cannot represent Breda's physical utility, facility or supply topology.
findings.evidence: Ten NWB-derived crossings with total nominal logical capacity 2,160 connect GM0758 to seven neighbours. The engine applies the same A16/A27/A58/A59/N263/N282/N285/N639 records to power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply. E03/E06/E08 establish discipline-specific providers, assets and dependencies, not shared road topology. The engine/UI correctly emit transferSemantics logical-proxy, but direction, capacity and flow are not feeders, pipes, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food/fuel routes.
findings.action: Keep logical-proxy language and prevent these flows from supporting physical claims. Restrict NWB/NDW to mobility and repair/supply access; add utility/facility edges only from operator-authorized topology or clearly named editable exercise gateways with capacity and live state Unknown by default.

findings.summary: Breda's highway/rail hub and published flooded-road classes are static context and do not drive first-72-hour access or dependencies.
findings.evidence: E02 and the deployed data identify ten major/regional boundary crossings, Breda and Breda Prinsenbeek stations and 237 GTFS stop areas; E03 identifies region-wide road, rail and hazardous-material dependencies. E04 explicitly classifies roads as normal, emergency-only at 10–30 cm or impassable at 30 cm and above under its modeled cloudburst. The simulation uses logical municipal endpoints but no climate-road geometry, current timetable trip, NDW event/closure/speed, evacuation throughput, response route, rail interruption or repair access. Compound mobility availability 0.408439 at both T+24 and T+72 is therefore a scenario balance, not an observed network state.
findings.action: Integrate E04 road-passability geometry only for its resolved rainfall scenario, and NDW DATEX II CC0 event-valid closures/incidents/traffic with publication/validity time for observed context. Keep ProRail/GTFS as dated infrastructure/schedule context and never infer disaster-time passenger or emergency capacity from stations/stops.

findings.summary: Provider polygons, antennas, schools, Amphia and demographic aggregates do not resolve first-72-hour utility, care or household continuity.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and remote coastal/wildfire effects are bounded exercises but not locally calibrated Breda forecasts or probabilities.

findings.summary: The deterministic ten-scenario contract, zero-intensity baseline, causal ledgers, reconciliation and sustained-water recovery guard pass for GM0758.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passed 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services. All zero-intensity runs were exactly zero for severity, peak, affected population and cumulative event-attributable person-hours; repeated frames, finite bounds, monotonic accumulation and route bounds passed. Compound T+24 reconciles 188,779 people, 127,951 affected and every demand/delivery ledger within 2.84e-14; all eleven map layers are invariant. Active river/compound water holds every service recoveryProgress at zero through T+72. Explanations label person-hours, operational multipliers, interventions and road-derived transfers as scenario/proxy semantics.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Breda disaster, outage, casualty, evacuation, welfare or restoration dataset.
The 2025 generalized CBS boundary is suitable for municipal aggregation but not parcel-level hydraulics, asset ownership, response jurisdiction or exact incident geometry.

Breda's wateroverlast/hitte ArcGIS services are modeled stress/context layers; event wording conflicts for the water raster, centre-point identify is not zonal analysis, NoData is common, and licence/cadence must be cleared before ingestion.

Official Markdal, regional-defence, watercourse and asset registers do not prove hydraulic connection, defence failure, water depth, arrival, duration or recession; an expert must select and version a physically relevant event.
TOP10NL forest cover and the provincial Mastbos committee are static context rather than live fuel, moisture, wind-driven spread, suppression or access state; the focused ignition is synthetic.
HWH/provider/antenna/facility/station/GTFS records are partial dated context, not complete topology, capacity, operating state, backup, stock or restoration commitments.
No reviewed public safe source provides complete Enexis, Brabant Water, municipal sewer, gas, telecom, Amphia, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behavior, medically dependent people, responders, mutual aid, shelters, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, crew travel, repair priorities, cross-border Belgium flows and visitor/daytime demand remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
